newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed on uncertainty.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed on uncertainty.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trading on Monday, with the short-term market trend unclear, traders said.
The key January 1997 contract ended at 3,205 yuan ($386) per tonne, up 11 yuan. It opened at 3,205 and stayed at that level for the whole session.
March rose 13 to 3,240 and May one to 3,329, July fell three to 3,378, September dropped two to 3,378 and November rose two to 3,400.
Combined volume was 12,900 tonnes, unchanged from that of Friday.
Traders said many investors remained on the sidelines due to an uncertain short-term market trend.
"Many investors did not want to enter the soybean market due to a lack of market-moving news," one trader said.
"Soybean is likely to continue moving around the 3,200-yuan level and is waiting for market-moving factors in the short term," he added.
Traders expect investors to take a wait-and-see attitude.
